item.title: IBC: New Chairperson takes charge at IBBI
item.description:
IBC · Press release

Who it covers: All stakeholders under the Code.

  • A new Chairperson took charge of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India on 26-11-2026.
  • A new ex-officio member was notified on 04-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Disciplinary orders: three insolvency professionals suspended for two years each
item.description:
IBC · Enforcement order

Who it covers: Insolvency professionals; creditors' committees that appoint them.

  • The IBBI Disciplinary Committee suspended the registration of three insolvency professionals for two years each, by orders of 03-11-2026, 12-11-2026 and 13-11-2026.
  • A suspended professional cannot continue existing assignments (section 206), so the creditors must replace them.
  • A fourth order of 09-11-2026 concerned the conduct of a liquidation, including valuation and a scheme placed without secured creditors' consent.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Real estate CIRPs: RERA compliance, RERA's views on plans and site notices
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/CIRP/110/2026

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: IRPs and RPs of corporate debtors with real estate projects, CoCs and prospective resolution applicants.

  • RPs must comply with RERA during the CIRP.
  • RPs may invite RERA's written views on plans and share them with the CoC and bidders.
  • The CIRP must be shown on signboards at each project site and office within 7 days of appointment.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Revised Form CA with a separate part for homebuyers
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/CIRP/109/2026

Effective 2026-10-30.

Who it covers: Financial creditors in a class, including real estate allottees, and IRPs and RPs.

  • Form CA has Part I for other creditors in a class and Part II for allottees.
  • Claims filed earlier need not be refiled.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Liquidator may modify the list of stakeholders and tells the NCLT within 30 days
item.description:
IBC · Regulation · IBBI/2026-27/GN/REG154

Effective 2026-09-22.

Who it covers: Liquidators and stakeholders in liquidation.

  • The liquidator may modify an entry in the list of stakeholders on new information and informs the NCLT within 30 days.

Official source

item.title: IBC: No interim moratorium for personal guarantors, even in pending applications
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/II/106/2026

Effective 2026-09-21.

Who it covers: Creditors of personal guarantors, resolution professionals and guarantors.

  • IBBI drew attention to Bombay and Delhi High Court rulings that the 2026 amendment ended the interim moratorium for personal guarantors from 26-05-2026, including for applications pending then.

Official source

item.title: IBC: IPs to watch for misuse of insolvency and apply to the NCLT
item.description:
IBC · Circular · IBBI/CIRP/105/2026

Effective 2026-09-09.

Who it covers: Insolvency professionals; creditors and debtors in CIRPs and liquidations.

  • IBBI listed signs of misuse, such as a single non-bank creditor dominating the CoC, clusters of connected companies and very low recoveries without proper valuation.
  • An IP who believes on reasonable grounds that a process is fraudulent or malicious must apply to the NCLT.

Official source

item.title: IBC: Observers in CoCs dominated by non-bank creditors
item.description:
IBC · Regulation · IBBI/2026-27/GN/REG153

Effective 2026-06-09.

Who it covers: CoCs where creditors other than scheduled banks and public financial institutions hold over 66% of the vote.

  • The RP invites the five largest unrelated operational creditors, including the three largest statutory authorities, as non-voting observers and minutes their views.
  • Only unrelated operational creditors count for a CoC made only of operational creditors.

Official source

item.title: IBC: IBBI regulations aligned with the 2026 Code amendments
item.description:
IBC · Regulation · IBBI/2026-27/GN/REG144 to REG152

Effective 2026-06-02.

Who it covers: All processes under the Code.

  • Liquidation to finish within 180 days; secured creditors decide within 14 days; claims verified within 7 days; distribution within 15 days.
  • CIRP claims admitted or rejected with reasons within 7 days; more information required with s. 9 and s. 10 applications.
  • Forms are now notified by IBBI circular (formats circulars of 02-06-2026 and 03-06-2026).

Official source

item.title: IBC: IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 in force (except CIIRP and group insolvency)
item.description:
IBC · Act · Act 6 of 2026; S.O. 2625(E)

Effective 2026-05-26.

Who it covers: Everyone dealing with processes under the Code.

  • Admission of a financial creditor's application is mandatory once default is shown; an IU record of default suffices for a financial institution.
  • Withdrawal needs 90% of the CoC and is barred after the first invitation for plans.
  • CoC supervises liquidation; CIRP can be restored for up to 120 days; dissolution without liquidation.
  • Government dues are not treated as secured in the waterfall.
  • No interim moratorium for personal guarantors.
  • New penalties for frivolous proceedings and breach of moratorium or plan.

Official source

item.title: IBC: International Valuation Standards apply to valuations under the Code

Effective 2026-04-01.
